subject: CI gate & secret chain-of-custody for SIG review
messages:
From: Claire Reynolds <auditor@clarity-assess.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: security@finbank.com
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG: Request — CI gate & secrets chain-of-custody

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this on. For FinBank's SIG submission we need a focused package describing how code changes make it to production and how secrets are handled during that flow. Specifically:

- A concise description of the merge/approval gate (who approves, automated checks, blocking criteria).
- Evidence of CI runs blocking on failed secret scans / policy violations (logs or annotated runs).
- Proof of KMS key rotation and who performed/authorized the rotations over the last 12 months.
- Chain-of-custody for artifact signing (where the signing key lives, who signs, timestamped records).

If you can provide a short write-up plus a few artifacts (CI run IDs, rotation log, signing proof) that would be ideal. FinBank would like this by EOD Wednesday if possible.

Claire 
Claire Reynolds
Senior Assessor — Clarity Assessment

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Claire Reynolds <auditor@clarity-assess.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: Request — CI gate & secrets chain-of-custody

Hi Claire,

Thanks — we can do that. I'll pull a compact bundle that maps each requested item to exact artifacts and run IDs. Monica will extract the CI runs and the secret-scan failures; Jonas will pull KMS rotation history and signing proofs.

Quick clarifications:
- Do you need raw CI logs, or is annotated excerpts (timestamp + pipeline stage + link) sufficient?
- For KMS rotation proof, is a CSV with rotation timestamps and key IDs OK, or do you need signed attestation from our security team?

I'll aim to deliver the write-up and attachments by Wed 18:00 PT.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: Request — CI gate & secrets chain-of-custody

Hey team,

I pulled the CI excerpts and annotated them. Attached: ci_pipeline_runbook.pdf (explains each pipeline stage and the merge-gate logic), and merge-gate-approval-log.csv (recent approvals and approvers). Key points:

- Merge gate is enforced by the repo branch policy + CI stage 'policy-check'. PRs require: 2 code-owner approvals OR 1 code-owner + security sign-off for risky subsystems.
- policy-check runs: unit tests, lint, dependency-scan, secret-scan (detects high-entropy strings / known patterns), infra-policy checks. Any failure blocks merge.
- We keep pipeline run IDs in our internal trace; examples included as run IDs in the runbook (links in Drive).

Attachments: ci_pipeline_runbook.pdf (4 pages), merge-gate-approval-log.csv (last 90 days, csv).

Monica
Monica Patel
Engineering Manager, CI Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments (stubbed):
- ci_pipeline_runbook.pdf (application/pdf)
- merge-gate-approval-log.csv (text/csv)

Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 10:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: Request — CI gate & secrets chain-of-custody

Folks,

I've exported the KMS rotation history and artifact-signing proof. See attached: kms_rotation_audit.csv (rotation_id, key_id, rotated_at, rotated_by, approver), artifact-signing-proof.txt (hashes + timestamps + signer identity). Notes:

- Rotations are automated monthly for ephemeral signing keys, and yearly for root-of-trust keys; all rotations are triggered by our key-ops job and require an Ops approval ticket for root rotations.
- For signing, we use a hardware-backed signing service in our VPC; signing events are logged with full timestamps and the signing cert. The attached proof shows the artifact hash and the signing cert thumbprint.
- Links to Drive bundle: https://redwood-inference.drive/FinBank/SIG/CI-Gate-2026 (read-only for assessor).

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Claire / FinBank team,

Attached is the package for your SIG review. Summary of artifacts delivered and mapping to your asks: 

1) Merge/approval gate: ci_pipeline_runbook.pdf (see 'policy-check' section) + merge-gate-approval-log.csv (proves approver identities and timestamps).
2) CI block evidence: run excerpts are referenced in the runbook with three sample failing runs (IDs: 84721, 85903, 87012) where secret-scan blocked merge; raw logs are on Drive if you need them.
3) KMS rotation proof: kms_rotation_audit.csv includes key IDs and rotation timestamps for the past 12 months; root rotations show approval ticket numbers.
4) Artifact signing chain-of-custody: artifact-signing-proof.txt includes artifact hashes and signer cert thumbprints. The signing key is HSM-backed (on-prem VPC) and access requires key-ops approval.

Links: https://redwood-inference.drive/FinBank/SIG/CI-Gate-2026

Attachments (included in Drive bundle): ci_pipeline_runbook.pdf, merge-gate-approval-log.csv, kms_rotation_audit.csv, artifact-signing-proof.txt

Thanks,

Hi Priyom — thanks for the rapid turnaround. I downloaded the bundle and spot-checked the runs and rotation CSV. This is exactly the mapping we need for the SIG intake. Two quick follow-ups: 

1) Can you provide a redacted raw CI log for run 84721 showing the secret-scan failure (we only need the section with the failure lines and metadata).
2) If possible, include a short signed attestation from your security lead confirming the HSM-backed signing process and the rotation policy (one paragraph).

If you can get those by Friday EOD GMT we'll be able to mark this item as satisfied in the intake tracker.

Appreciate the help — Claire
Claire Reynolds
